Crucially, quarterly operating margins have dramatically improved by 33 percentage points, rising to -7% in September 2026 from -40% in the year-ago quarter [E23]. This operational recovery is backed by positive operating cash flow of Rs 3 Cr for March 2026 [E27] and robust medium-term growth, boasting a 17% compounded sales growth rate over 5 years [E12]. Furthermore, the broader macroeconomic backdrop provides strong tailwinds, with the textiles sector scoring a positive tailwind reading [E43, E45] and accelerating results showing net profit up 42% year-on-year [E44]. The company's solvency and profitability are severely compromised, evidenced by a dismal Return on Assets (ROA) of -14.52% and Return on Capital Employed (ROCE) of -13.93%, both lagging far behind sector benchmarks [E7, E9]. Furthermore, operations are cash-destructive on a net basis, producing a heavy Free Cash Flow burn of ₹ -34 Cr for March 2026 alongside rising borrowings of ₹ 193 Cr and a flagged low interest coverage ratio [E28, E29, E37]. Long-term growth metrics remain anaemic, with compounded profit growth contracting by -6% over 3 years and crashing by -191% over the trailing twelve months [E16, E17]. Market sentiment reflects these underlying distress signals, as domestic institutional holding has been completely liquidated to 0.00% and the stock languishes near the bottom of its 52-week range at just 13% of its span [E4, E32]. Furthermore, the bull points to positive operating cash flow [E27], but ignores the severe capital hemorrhage of ₹ -34 Cr in free cash flow as of Mar 2026 [E28], alongside rising borrowings of ₹ 193 Cr that leave the company explicitly flagged for a low interest coverage ratio [E29, E37]. Finally, the broader textile sector tailwind [E45] fails to validate the company's performance, given that its abysmal ROCE of -13.93% and ROA of -14.52% drastically underperform sector medians [E7, E9, E48].
